1.q: הַ⁠דָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵ⁠אֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה
1.note: Jeremiah is using the phrase translated as **The word that was to Jeremiah from Yahweh** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

2.q: שִׁמְע֕וּ אֶת דִּבְרֵ֖י הַ⁠בְּרִ֣ית הַ⁠זֹּ֑את וְ⁠דִבַּרְתָּ⁠ם֙
2.note: The imperative **Listen to** is plural, because Yahweh is addressing the people of Judah, but the imperative translated as **speak** is singular, because Yahweh is addressing Jeremiah himself. Use the plural and singular forms in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

The word translated as **men** is singular in form, but it represents all the people of Judah as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a word or phrase that refers to the whole group. Alternate translation: [the people of Judah]
By **Listen to**, Yahweh means “pay attention to.” Alternate translation: [Pay attention to]

3.q: וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵי⁠הֶ֔ם כֹּֽה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אָר֣וּר הָ⁠אִ֔ישׁ
3.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and tell them that Yahweh, the God of Israel, says that he will curse the man]

The expression **Cursed is** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I curse the man]

3.q: הָ⁠אִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁמַ֔ע אֶת דִּבְרֵ֖י הַ⁠בְּרִ֥ית הַ⁠זֹּֽאת
3.note: Yahweh is not referring to a specific **man**. He means men in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [is anyone who does not hear the words of this covenant]

4.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of the earlier generations of the people of Judah as if they were the **fathers** of the people he is addressing. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your forefathers]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the suffering that the Israelites experienced in Egypt as if it were **the furnace of iron**, a fire hot enough to melt iron. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from the place where they suffered terribly]

4.q: לֵ⁠אמֹ֗ר שִׁמְע֤וּ בְ⁠קוֹלִ⁠י֙ וַ⁠עֲשִׂיתֶ֣ם אוֹתָ֔⁠ם כְּ⁠כֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר אֲצַוֶּ֖ה אֶתְ⁠כֶ֑ם
4.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [telling them to listen to my voice and to do according to all that I commanded them, so they would be to me for a people, and I would be to them for God]

Here, **my voice** represents what Yahweh commands. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Listen to what I command]
See how you translated “listen” in 3:13. Alternate translation: [Pay attention to my voice]

5.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of the productivity of the land as if the land were **flowing of milk and honey**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a land that produces abundant food]

Jeremiah is using the two verbs **answered** and **said** together to indicate that what follows is a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.

The implication is that Jeremiah is expressing his agreement with everything that Yahweh has just said, both the curse and the promise. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [I agree with all that you have said, Yahweh]

7.note: Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **warned** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [For I earnestly warned your ancestors]

Yahweh is using **rising early and admonishing** as a common expression of the culture to mean “warning persistently and urgently.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [warning them persistently and urgently]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [telling them to listen to my voice]

8.note: Yahweh is using **incline their ear** as a common expression of the culture to mean “pay attention.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they did not heed me]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the way the people conducted their lives as if they **walked** along a path. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [but everyone lived according to the stubbornness of their evil heart]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **stubbornness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [stubbornly, according to their evil heart]

Here, **heart** represents the will and the inner attitude of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [their evil will]

8.q: וָ⁠אָבִ֨יא עֲלֵי⁠הֶ֜ם אֶֽת־כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֧י הַ⁠בְּרִית־הַ⁠זֹּ֛את אֲשֶׁר־צִוִּ֥יתִי לַ⁠עֲשׂ֖וֹת
8.note: Yahweh is using the term **words** to represent what he commanded by using words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Therefore I brought upon them the punishment that this covenant said would happen if they did not do everything that I commanded them to do]

9.note: The expression **has been found** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I have found a conspiracy among the men of Judah]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **conspiracy**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [A group that plots together]

10.q: אֲשֶׁ֤ר מֵֽאֲנוּ֙ לִ⁠שְׁמ֣וֹעַ אֶת דְּבָרַ֔⁠י וְ⁠הֵ֣מָּה הָלְכ֗וּ אַחֲרֵ֛י אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים
10.note: This could mean: (1) the pronoun **they** refers to present generation of the people of Judah, who have returned to the same sins the **first fathers**, or (2) the pronoun refers to the earlier generations who refused to obey Yahweh . It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [who refused to listen to my words, and those ancestors walked after other gods]

10.q: וְ⁠הֵ֣מָּה הָלְכ֗וּ אַחֲרֵ֛י אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים לְ⁠עָבְדָ֑⁠ם
10.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of giving loyalty and worship to other gods as if the people **walked after** those gods. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they followed other gods to serve them]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the people of Israel and the people of Judah as if each nation were a **house**, that is, a single family living together. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The nation of Israel and the nation of Judah]

10.q: אֶת בְּרִיתִ֕⁠י אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּרַ֖תִּי אֶת אֲבוֹתָֽ⁠ם
10.note: Yahweh is using the word **cut** as a common expression of the culture to mean “made,” since people in this culture cut animals in pieces when they made a covenant. If this word does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my covenant that I established with their fathers]

11.q: לָ⁠כֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְ⁠נִ֨י מֵבִ֤יא אֲלֵי⁠הֶם֙ רָעָ֔ה
11.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Therefore I, Yahweh, say that I am indeed bringing calamity to them]

Yahweh is using **Behold me** as an expression that people of this culture would commonly use to mean that they were about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Now I am about to bring calamity]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **calamity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [disastrous events]

It might seem that the expression **which they will not be able to go out from it** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [from which they will not be able to go out]

12.q: וְ⁠הָֽלְכ֞וּ עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה וְ⁠יֹשְׁבֵי֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְ⁠זָֽעֲקוּ֙
12.note: Here, **the cities of Judah** represents the people who live in those cities. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Then the people of the cities of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem will go and cry out]

The implication is that the people were burning incense and presenting sacrifices to these gods in order to worship them. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [are burning incense as offerings to worship them]

It might seem that the expression **to whom they are offering to them** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [to whom they are offering sacrifices]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **save** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [but they will certainly not save them at all]

13.q: כִּ֚י מִסְפַּ֣ר עָרֶ֔י⁠ךָ הָי֥וּ אֱלֹהֶ֖י⁠ךָ יְהוּדָ֑ה וּ⁠מִסְפַּ֞ר חֻצ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם שַׂמְתֶּ֤ם מִזְבְּחוֹת֙ לַ⁠בֹּ֔שֶׁת מִזְבְּח֖וֹת לְ⁠קַטֵּ֥ר לַ⁠בָּֽעַל
13.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [For you have countless gods and altars, Judah — one for every city and every street in Jerusalem — where you offer to that shameful thing, Baal]

Even though Yahweh has previously been speaking about the people of Judah, here he turns and addresses them directly, saying **your cities** and **your gods**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could continue to speak about them in the third person here. Alternate translation: [as the number of the cities of the people of Judah are their gods]

Here, **shameful thing** represents the false god Baal, whose worship brought shame upon the people who worshiped him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to that disgraceful god]

14.note: The word translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [Because of this, you]
The pronoun **you** refers to Jeremiah, not to the people of Judah. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Therefore you, Jeremiah,]

Yahweh is using **lift up a cry or a prayer** as a common expression of the culture to mean “pray earnestly.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and do not earnestly beg me to help them]

15.q: מֶ֣ה לִֽ⁠ידִידִ֞⁠י בְּ⁠בֵיתִ֗⁠י עֲשׂוֹתָ֤⁠הּ הַֽ⁠מְזִמָּ֨תָ⁠ה֙ הָֽ⁠רַבִּ֔ים וּ⁠בְשַׂר קֹ֖דֶשׁ יַעַבְר֣וּ מֵֽ⁠עָלָ֑יִ⁠ךְ
15.note: Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke the people of Judah for coming to his temple while they continue to do wicked things. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [My beloved has no right to be in my house, since she does her many wicked deeds, and the flesh of the holy offering cannot take your guilt away from you!]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [What right does my beloved have to be in my house]

Yahweh actually means to communicate the opposite of the literal meaning of what he is saying here. He is not asking what right his beloved has in his house, but rather saying that she has forfeited that right. If a speaker of your language would not do that, you could translate the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [My beloved has no right to be in my house]

Here, **my house** represents the temple in Jerusalem. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the temple where I dwell]

15.q: עֲשׂוֹתָ֤⁠הּ הַֽ⁠מְזִמָּ֨תָ⁠ה֙ הָֽ⁠רַבִּ֔ים וּ⁠בְשַׂר קֹ֖דֶשׁ יַעַבְר֣וּ מֵֽ⁠עָלָ֑יִ⁠ךְ
15.note: The pronoun **her** and the pronoun **you** both refer to the people of Judah, whom Yahweh has just called his beloved. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [to do the wickedness of the people of Judah … they pass over from the people of Judah]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **wickedness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to do what is wicked]

Yahweh is using the adjective **the many** as a noun to mean a certain kind of people. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [many people]

The implication is that this refers to the meat of the animals that the people sacrificed at the temple. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the meat of the sacrificed animals]

This could mean: (1) that the people of Judah rejoice when they do what is evil. Alternate translation: [When you do what is evil, then you rejoice] or (2) that the people of Judah exult when disaster comes. Alternate translation: [Can holy meat prevent your disaster so that you can celebrate?]

16.note: Yahweh is using **called your name** as a common expression of the culture to mean “gave you the name.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh gave you the name]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the people of Judah as if they were a **leafy olive tree** that was **beautiful** and produced good fruit. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a people like a leafy olive tree, beautiful and full of good fruit]

16.q: לְ⁠ק֣וֹל הֲמוּלָּ֣ה גְדֹלָ֗ה הִצִּ֥ית אֵשׁ֙ עָלֶ֔י⁠הָ וְ⁠רָע֖וּ דָּלִיּוֹתָֽי⁠ו
16.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of the judgment that he will bring on the people of Judah as if it were **a fire** that would burn that olive tree and break its **branches**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [With the noise of a great storm, he will destroy her completely, and her people will be shattered]

The pronoun **he** refers to Yahweh, and the pronoun **her** refers to the olive tree, which represents the people of Judah. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will kindle a fire upon that olive tree, the people of Judah]

The expression **will be broken** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and the kindled fire will break its branches]

17.q: וַ⁠יהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ הַ⁠נּוֹטֵ֣עַ אוֹתָ֔⁠ךְ דִּבֶּ֥ר עָלַ֖יִ⁠ךְ רָעָ֑ה
17.note: Yahweh is speaking about himself in the third person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [For I, Yahweh of Armies, the one who planted you, have spoken calamity against you]

Here Yahweh is speaking of establishing the people of Israel and Judah in their land as if he had **planted** them like a tree. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the one who established you in your land]

Yahweh is using **spoken calamity against you** as a common expression of the culture to mean “decreed that disaster will come upon you.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [has decreed that disaster will come upon you]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe the **evil** that **the house of Israel and the house of Judah** have committed. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the wicked things that the house of Israel and the house of Judah have done]

18.note: The implication is that what Yahweh made known to Jeremiah was that his enemies were plotting to kill him. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh made known to me the plot against my life, and so I knew about it]

Jeremiah has been speaking about Yahweh in the third person, but here he addresses Yahweh directly in the second person as **you**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could continue to speak about Yahweh in the third person here. Alternate translation: [then he showed me their deeds]

The implication is that **their deeds** are the actions of the men of Anathoth, Jeremiah’s own townspeople. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [then you showed me the deeds of the men of Anathoth]

19.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a gentle lamb** does not know that it is being led away to be killed, so Jeremiah did not know that his enemies were plotting to kill him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [And I was as unsuspecting as a gentle lamb being led away to be killed]

The expression **brought to slaughter** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that people lead away to kill]

19.q: עָלַ֣⁠י חָשְׁב֣וּ מַחֲשָׁב֗וֹת נַשְׁחִ֨יתָה עֵ֤ץ בְּ⁠לַחְמ⁠וֹ֙
19.note: Jeremiah is reporting the words of his enemies directly, without using a verb of speaking to introduce them. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language. Alternate translation: [and they said]

The enemies of Jeremiah are using **cut him off from the land of the living** as a common expression of the culture to mean “kill him.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And let us put him to death]

The expression **will not be remembered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that no one will mention his name any longer]

Here, **his name** represents Jeremiah himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [that he will not be remembered any longer]

20.note: Jeremiah is using the possessive form to describe **one judging** who is characterized by **righteousness**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [is a righteous judge]

Here, **kidneys and the heart** represents the innermost thoughts and emotions of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [examining the inner thoughts and feelings]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **vengeance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Let me see you avenge me on them]

21.q: לָ⁠כֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ עַל אַנְשֵׁ֣י עֲנָת֔וֹת הַֽ⁠מְבַקְשִׁ֥ים אֶֽת נַפְשְׁ⁠ךָ֖ לֵ⁠אמֹ֑ר
21.note: Jeremiah is using the word **saying** to introduce what the men of Anathoth said to him, not what Yahweh said. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.
The word **Anathoth** is the name of a town.

Yahweh is using **seeking your life** as a common expression of the culture to mean “trying to kill you.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [who are trying to kill you]

Here, **the name of Yahweh** represents the authority of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Do not prophesy with Yahweh’s authority]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **die**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [and you will remain alive]

Here, **our hand** represents the power of the men of Anathoth to kill Jeremiah. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and then we will not kill you]

22.note: Yahweh is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation.
Here, **the sword** represents warfare. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [The young men will die in battle]

23.note: Yahweh is using **year of their visitation** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the time when I will punish them.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [at the time when I punish them]
